hook.text: A tension setting squeezes the stone.

lines.text: A tension setting squeezes the stone.
It holds the stone with no prongs and no bezel.
Tiny grooves in the two band ends hold the stone's edge.
The springy band presses on the stone from both sides.
The jeweler springs the band open and sets the stone.
When released, the metal springs back and grips it.
Each ring is made to order for one stone.
Only hard stones work, about 9 on the Mohs scale or more.
lines.say: Only hard stones work, about nine on the Mohs scale or more.

lines.text: Makers cite about 12,000 pounds of pressure per square inch.
lines.say: Makers cite about twelve thousand pounds of pressure per square inch.

lines.text: Resizing is very hard, and a hard knock can loosen the stone.
So a tension setting holds a stone by squeezing, not with prongs.
A render shows how the ring looks before anything is cast.

post.caption: A tension setting holds a stone with the squeeze of the metal band instead of prongs. Tiny grooves in the two band ends hold the stone's edge, and the springy band presses on it from both sides. Each ring is made to order for one hard stone, and it is very hard to resize.
